newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq ends with record point rise as techs surge.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq ends with record point rise as techs surge.

text.p: Technology stocks surged amid active trading on Wednesday, pushing the Nasdaq to a record point rise.
"The techs were extremely strong," said one trader. "All the bid leaders were up."
The broad rally extended across the board from chip stocks to networks to computers.

The Nasdaq composite index ended 38.52 points or 2.50 percent higher to an unofficial close of 1580.63. The last time the index had such a point rise was May 2, 1997, when it went up 34.83. Advancing issues led decliners six to five on a huge volume of 848.7 million shares.
"There was a lot of covering of shorts," said another trader. "It should follow up tomorrow, but there will be some profit-taking at some point."
Intel Corp was the most active stock, ending 7-15/32 higher at 88-3/8 after a strong earnings report.

Andrew Corp ended 5-5/8 down at 27-3/8 after Cowen & Co downgraded it to buy from strong buy. Andrew also reported earnings of $0.08 a share, blaming sluggishness in the personal communications market for a decline in sales.
